newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stock exchange relaxes trading norms.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stock exchange relaxes trading norms.

text.p: The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) said on Friday it has relaxed the ceiling on outstanding businesses for the least actively traded stocks.

The ceiling on net and gross cumulative outstanding positions in B2 group shares have been raised to 1.0 million rupees and 7.5 million respectively from 750,000 rupees and 5.0 million, the BSE said in a note.

In the case of Bank of Baroda and Dena Bank, two state-run banks listed in the past four months, the BSE has allowed net cumulative positions of 2.0 million rupees subject to the overall gross business of 7.5 million.
The higher limits are effective immediately, it said.
"Keeping in view the improved market conditions, it has been decided to increase the above limits," the note said.

Net cumulative business is the difference betweem purchases and sales in any one stock by each member-broker. Gross positions are the total of purchases and sales in all stocks taken together by a broker.
The B2 group comprises of shares which are not very actively traded.
